answer: A website I find genuinely useful is an online learning platform that offers courses on almost any subject imaginable. I use it regularly to develop new skills related to my work and personal interests. Over the past year, for instance, I have done a course on digital marketing, which helps with promoting our consultancy, and another on advanced spreadsheets. I usually log on three or four evenings a week, for about an hour, and a bit longer on Fridays. What makes it so useful is how [[accessible]] it makes education; I can learn from experts around the world without leaving my home. That matters a lot when you live in a smaller town like Sirajganj, where specialist training is hard to find. I have taken several courses on it, and the quality of instruction has been genuinely impressive, with clear videos, short quizzes and forums where you can ask questions and get answers from other learners. It fits perfectly around my busy schedule, since I can learn at my own pace whenever I have free time. Honestly, I think platforms like this are [[revolutionising]] the way people learn. They [[democratise]] knowledge that was once available only to a privileged few. I find it incredibly [[empowering]] to be able to keep learning and improving myself so easily. In a rapidly changing world where continuous learning is essential, I think tools like this are [[invaluable]]. It has genuinely helped me grow both professionally and personally, and I recommend it to everyone, especially students preparing to study abroad.

followUps.q: Have you ever paid for an online course?
followUps.answer: Yes, a couple of times, when I needed a proper certificate. Most of what I learn is free, but paying for a course actually makes me more committed, because I don't want to waste the money.

followUps.q: Is online learning as good as learning in a classroom?
followUps.answer: For practical skills, I think it is almost as good. But a classroom gives you spontaneous discussion and a teacher who notices when you are confused, which is hard to [[replicate]] online.
